parsed.narrative: With the default choices dark-skinned players are carded more: OR 1.34 (95% CI 1.13 to 1.58), p = 0.0006, n = 124,621 dyads, so the verdict is BIAS DETECTED. None of the 9 single-decision changes reverses it: the odds ratio stays between 1.27 and 1.36 and every interval keeps excluding 1. None of the 10 pairs ranked most likely to flip it does either. The verdict first changes at three simultaneous changes: 4 such universes reach NO CLEAR EVIDENCE, with odds ratios of 1.20 to 1.25 and p between 0.055 and 0.069. All of them adjust for the full covariate set, and most add player-clustered errors and the second rater alone. The minimal flip (second rater only, referees with 22 or more dyads, full covariates; OR 1.20 (95% CI 1.00 to 1.46), p = 0.055) was re-executed from a fresh sandbox and reproduced exactly. Across all defensible universes the odds ratio runs from 1.20 to 1.36, inside the human teams' range of 0.89 to 2.93. The only one-decision change that did flip the verdict, keeping low-bias referees only (OR 1.25 (95% CI 0.99 to 1.59), p = 0.066), was rejected as an indefensible change of population.
caveats: Odds ratios compare the lightest with the darkest tone on a 0 to 1 scale and rest on player-referee dyads, not on individual refereeing decisions.
The estimate is an association; it cannot separate bias from unmeasured differences in playing style or match context.
Influence is measured under fixed defaults and is not a causal statement about the world.
